sections.h2: Can a Plantation, FL homeowner get a quick cash sale?
sections.html:
Yes. A cash buyer can purchase a Plantation house without waiting for a lender, so the timeline depends on the title search, any payoffs and the deed signing. A traditional listing adds an appraisal, an inspection round and loan approval for the buyer.

Plantation is centered in Broward County, directly west of Fort Lauderdale and about 20 miles north of Miami-Dade County. The city's demographics page lists a 2018 population of 94,288 on 22.8 square miles and says home values range from $125,000 to over $2 million, with a median value of $271,200 in that count. The figures date from 2018, so use them for context and check current values with the Broward County Property Appraiser.

  • Cash suits a house with deferred repairs, code issues or a tenant.
  • A listing suits a house that shows well in a season of strong demand.
  • Estates and liens need paperwork under either path.

sections.h2: How did Plantation's founding plan shape its lots?
sections.html:
Frederick Peters bought 10,000 acres along State Road 7 in the 1930s and hired architect Russell Pancoast to plan a city. The plan barred homes next to each other from looking alike, set minimum lot sizes and divided land into residential, commercial and industrial zones. His idea of "long acres" offered one-acre lots with two thirds kept for gardens and fruit trees.

The city incorporated on April 30, 1953 with fewer than 500 people and a $1,288 budget, and its first council met on May 11, 1953 in an old feed warehouse near East Acre Drive and Broward Boulevard. The present city hall was dedicated in 1973. Annexations in the following decades stretched the city from State Road 7 to Flamingo Road, about seven miles, so the west side is newer than the east.

That layout explains why a Plantation Acres lot can look nothing like a house in the western neighborhoods. Tell buyers which part of the city you live in, since lot size and age of construction differ by area.

sections.h2: What are Plantation's climate, schools and jobs?
sections.html:
Plantation facts from the city's demographics page

ClimateSubtropical, 62 inches of rain a year
Average temperature75.4 degrees, winter mean 66.5, summer mean 84.2
Public schools6 elementary, 2 middle, 2 high
Private schools32, preschool through grade 12
JobsOver 5,000 registered businesses, over 47,000 persons employed
Parks42 parks and playgrounds on 642 acres, 6 golf courses

The city says 93.5 percent of residents have a high school diploma or higher and 41.4 percent hold a bachelor's degree or more. Median household income was $69,531 for the city and $52,954 for Broward County on its 2018 count, and median age was 39.7.

Employers named by the city include Motorola Solutions, National Beverage, Magic Leap, Florida Power and Light, DHL, Westside Regional Medical Center and Plantation General Hospital. Heavy rain and heat make roofs, drainage and cooling the questions a buyer's inspector asks first.

sections.h2: What closing charges apply to a Plantation deed?
sections.html:
Broward uses the standard 70 cents per $100 stamp tax. Miami-Dade, a short drive south, runs 60 cents plus a 45 cents surtax with a carve-out for single-family homes, so do not use a Miami-Dade quote for a Plantation deed.

The clerk charges $5.00 for the first recorded page and $4.00 for each additional page. Every party on the deed can be held liable for the tax, so write the payer into the contract.

sections.h2: How do Broward homestead rules and caps affect me?
sections.html:
A resident owner who occupied the house on January 1 can apply by March 1 for a homestead exemption of up to $50,000. After the first year, yearly growth in assessed value is capped at the lower of 3 percent or inflation, and the state chart lists 2.9 percent for 2025 and 2.7 percent for 2026. Other property is limited to 10 percent a year.

The city's history page says Plantation has one of the lowest millage rates in Broward County. Treat that as a general statement and ask Broward's offices for the current figure for your address.

  • A sale triggers reassessment at market value for the buyer on the next January 1.
  • You may carry savings to a new Florida homestead through portability within three years.
  • A bill dispute goes to the value adjustment board process within the deadlines on your August notice.

sections.h2: What if my Plantation house has a foreclosure, an estate or a tenant?
sections.html:
Each one can still end in a sale. A clerk's foreclosure sale follows judgment by 20 to 35 days unless extended, and the winning bidder posts a 5 percent deposit. An estate of $150,000 or less can use summary administration, and Florida's own estate tax ended for deaths after 2004. A landlord uses a three-day notice for unpaid rent and 30 days to end a month-to-month tenancy.

Check with a Florida attorney before signing a deed on behalf of an estate or a person in default.

sections.h2: What steps does a Plantation sale follow?
sections.html:
1. Gather payoff letters, tax bill and tenant information.
  2. Review written offers for the price, closing day and repair terms.
  3. The title agent clears the record.
  4. You sign the deed with two witnesses.
  5. Broward's clerk records it and funds are released.

Keep your recorded deed with your tax records.

faqs.q: Which county records a Plantation deed?
faqs.a: Broward County. The city's demographics page lists Broward as its county.

faqs.q: Why do Plantation lot sizes vary so much?
faqs.a: The city grew from a 1930s master plan with minimum lot sizes and later annexed western land out to Flamingo Road, so older and newer areas differ.

faqs.q: Is Plantation's deed tax the same as Miami-Dade's?
faqs.a: No. Broward uses 70 cents per $100, while Miami-Dade uses 60 cents plus a 45 cents surtax.

faqs.q: Does my homestead cap transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. A sale is a change of ownership, so the buyer starts at market value the following January 1.

faqs.q: Where can I find current Plantation population and home values?
faqs.a: Use the Broward County Property Appraiser for values. The city's demographics page lists population as of July 1, 2018, so it is background only.
